question_text: The time taken for a skier to complete a particular downhill run is normally distributed with mean $45\text{ seconds}$ and standard deviation $4\text{ seconds}$.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that the skier completes one downhill run in under 40 seconds.
subparts.solution:
Let the completion time of a randomly selected run be $X$ seconds.

$X \sim \text{N}(45, 4^2)$

$P(X < 40) \approx 0.106$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Evaluating lower tail of a normal distribution with mean $\mu=45$ and standard deviation $\sigma=4$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Entering variance $16$ as standard deviation instead of $4$.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that the skier completes two consecutive downhill runs in under 40 seconds each.

mark_breakdown.desc: Squaring the probability of a single run under 40 seconds

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Product rule for independent events: $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.
step_by_step: Take the probability of one run under 40 seconds: $p \approx 0.10565$.
Square the value for two independent consecutive runs: $p^2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Squaring the rounded value ($0.106^2 = 0.011236$) instead of using the unrounded value.

subparts.stem: The skier completes a total of 60 independent runs. How many times would you expect the run to take between 44 seconds and 47 seconds?

mark_breakdown.desc: Multiplying calculated probability by sample size $n = 60$
Rounding to the nearest whole number: 17 runs

subparts.solution:
$P(44 \le X \le 47) \approx 0.290$

$\therefore$ we expect about $0.290 \times 60 \approx 17$ runs to take between 44 seconds and 47 seconds.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Expected value of a binomial count: $\text{E}(Y) = n \times p$.
step_by_step: Multiply the probability by total number of runs: $60 \times 0.29017 \approx 17.41$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Leaving the expected number as a decimal without stating the integer approximation if whole counts are expected.
